t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a deep navy ground. Small wordmark and section label top-left, then a large two-line light-weight sans headline. One continuous double-line pipe in pale blue-white hairlines enters from the left edge and snakes across the width in two rows, carrying P&ID valve, pump and gauge symbols. At each symbol a mono number, a light uppercase title and a short caption sit beside the pipe for <CONTENT>. One steel-blue accent on the pipe. Flat line art, square corners, no shadows.
signature_idea: A single water route snakes across the section and every test point is a fitting on it, so the reader follows the water to each fault it can find.
strengths: one continuous pipe linking items is a clear, ownable device
light headline and navy blueprint palette are on-brand
P&ID symbols give real engineering vocabulary
route maps naturally to scroll-driven drawing
weaknesses: item numbers duplicated (02 and 04 appear twice) and copy repeated
reading order of the zigzag is confusing
pipe is pale, not steel-blue, so no accent leads
mixed icon styles (check badges, recycle arrows) clutter the drawing
dense, busy layout with too many captions
brand_fit_why: Navy blueprint, hairline pipe and light headline fit, but duplicated items, confusing order and cluttered icons undermine the calm and precision.
